A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGPO/SSAPO research, with matching authors, datasets, and principal experiments. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original SSAPO benchmark results, hyperparameter and seed-data analyses, and qualitative model outputs, including material in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original SSAPO results and additionally reports a seed-label-corruption experiment and an across-run variance finding.

M1.justification: The stated optimization procedure changes substantially: v1's iteration centered on the preceding adversary becomes an empirical-gap-centered follower with a proximal leader step. Section 3 and Algorithm 1 also specify margin-dependent support windows and revised leader weighting. These are procedural revisions beyond correcting the convexity terminology, although the unchanged implementation recipe in Appendix G.1 leaves their implementation unresolved.

E1.justification: UltraFeedback, UltraChat, AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, and the qualitative task examples remain. v3 adds a corrupted-supervision scenario using 25% flipped seed preference labels, extending noise-condition coverage without adding a dataset or benchmark.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same DPO, Iter-DPO, SPA, and Mistral reference comparators. However, v1's explicit numerical leaderboard comparison with Llama3-70B-Instruct in the introduction is removed. The new corruption experiment compares SSAPO conditions without adding a competing method.

E3.justification: v3 introduces an end-to-end rerun protocol comparing clean seeds with 25% label flips among the 2K seed pairs for both model families. The retained experiments keep their reported data splits, model configurations, metrics, sampling settings, and training hyperparameters.

E4.justification: v3 adds a controlled seed-label-noise test and a quantitative seed-selection stability finding. It removes v1 Table 6's three-seed-data sensitivity results and associated discussion. Radius, tangent-count, group-size, iteration, and qualitative analyses otherwise remain, including the unchanged iteration plot.

E5.justification: Appendix G.2 newly reports that farthest-point seed selection reduces performance variance across runs by approximately 40%. Neither a run count nor the underlying variances, confidence intervals, or estimation procedure is supplied. This adds uncertainty reporting without establishing that more runs were conducted.

E6.justification: Principal benchmark and retained ablation scores are unchanged. New Table 5 reports clean-to-corrupted LC/raw win rates of 26.90/31.93 to 19.70/18.51 for Mistral and 33.33/40.12 to 43.74/46.70 for LLaMA. v3 also adds the approximately 40% variance-reduction finding and removes the seed-specific results in v1 Table 6. The new Mistral clean control differs from Table 1 without an explained setting difference; it does not establish a version-to-version performance change.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendices C–F substantially revise the mathematics: explicit policy-dependent gap distributions replace the response-space formulation, the existence argument switches from Sion to Berge, convergence becomes local under additional assumptions, and Appendix D adds a center-stability assumption for the DPO lower bound. New results cover the unconstrained follower's closed form, convex piecewise-linear approximation, monotone tightening, and approximation/grouping/solver-error bounds.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain Stackelberg preference optimization, an O(epsilon) regret claim, and data-efficient self-annotation from 2K seed preferences. The introduction drops the specific claim of matching Llama3-70B-Instruct and uses broader competitive-performance language. This is a limited narrowing of the advertised comparison.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits robustness guarantees to training-time preference noise rather than jailbreaks or adversarial prompts. It adds a rationale for bounded-support finite optimization despite the unconstrained closed form, interprets LLaMA's improvement under label noise as regularization, and attributes excessive tangent counts to solver instability. The earlier seed-fluctuation explanation and adaptive-radius suggestion are removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, practical recommendations for epsilon, K, and G, and more explicit support-window and leader-update descriptions. Hardware, learning rates, beta values, generation limits, and timing information remain. Appendix G.1 still specifies the old tangents over [0,1], conflicting with the revised margin-space construction and limiting reproducibility.

R1.justification: v3 adds Berge and Aliprantis–Border references for the revised existence argument, while dropping Sion, Basar–Olsder, Cheng's adversarial preference optimization, and Wu's distributionally robust DPO references. Appendix A largely retains the positioning relative to SPA and policy-versus-policy alignment methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and theoretical/method sections undergo extensive rewriting and reorganization. The proof appendices are restructured, approximation effects receive a dedicated Appendix F, experimental details and examples move to G and H, and the impact statement moves to Appendix I. These changes substantially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document adopts a narrower NeurIPS layout with redesigned front matter, changed typography and headers, and widespread resizing and reflow. v1 Tables 4–5 become a combined v3 Table 4; the seed-data table disappears, and a corruption table and shaded hyperparameter box are added. Figure 2 is relocated and resized but uses the identical plot.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects v1's erroneous concavity description, adds direct noise testing, and clarifies robustness limitations. However, the revised algorithm introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Algorithm 1 defines sample weights as sums that Theorem 3.3 constrains to one, undermining the stated adversarial reweighting, while Appendix G.1 retains the conflicting old tangent construction. The new noise experiment also has an unexplained Mistral clean-control discrepancy. These benefits and central methodological ambiguities prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
